titulo: Things in the town, shops and shopping / Directions
descripcion_es: Places in the city, transport, and how to ask for and give directions.
resumen: Names of places and means of transport, and the basic phrases for asking where a place is and explaining how to get there.

explicacion.texto: To ask for directions, start with Excuse me and ask Where is…? or How do I get to…? To give them, use the imperative: go straight on, turn left, take the second street on the right.

filas: bank / post office
place for money / place for letters and parcels (es: banco / oficina de correos)
The post office is next to the bank.
chemist's / pharmacy
shop that sells medicine (es: farmacia)
Is there a chemist's near here?
town hall
building of the local government (es: ayuntamiento)
The town hall is in the main square.
square
open public space in a town (es: plaza)
Meet me in the square.
shopping centre
large building with many shops (es: centro comercial)
The new shopping centre is huge.
library
place where you borrow books (es: biblioteca)
I study at the library.
bookshop
shop that sells books (es: librería)
There's a great bookshop on this street.
underground / tube / subway
underground railway: British / London / American (es: metro)
Take the underground to the station.
bus stop
place where the bus stops (es: parada de autobús)
The bus stop is opposite the park.
traffic lights
red, amber and green lights for traffic (es: semáforo)
Turn right at the traffic lights.
roundabout
circular junction (es: rotonda)
Go round the roundabout.
crossroads
place where two roads cross (es: cruce)
Turn left at the crossroads.
Excuse me, where is…?
asking where a place is (es: Perdone, ¿dónde está…?)
Excuse me, where is the museum?
How do I get to…?
asking for the way (es: ¿Cómo llego a…?)
How do I get to the station?
go straight on / ahead
continue without turning (es: seguir todo recto)
Go straight on for two blocks.
turn left / right
change direction to the left / right (es: girar a la izquierda / derecha)
Turn left after the church.
take the first on the right
go into the first street on the right (es: coger la primera a la derecha)
Take the second on the left.
next to / opposite
beside / on the other side of the street (es: al lado de / enfrente de)
The café is opposite the cinema.
between / behind / in front of
in the middle of two things / at the back of / at the front of (es: entre / detrás de / delante de)
The car park is behind the hotel.
on the corner
where two streets meet (es: en la esquina)
There's a bakery on the corner.
It's a five-minute walk.
five minutes away walking (es: Está a cinco minutos andando.)
The beach is a ten-minute walk.
by bus / on foot
using the bus / walking (es: en autobús / a pie)
I go to work on foot.

items: Library is a place where you borrow books (es: biblioteca); a shop that sells books is a bookshop (false friend of Spanish “librería”).
Means of transport go with by: by car, by train; but on foot.
Opposite no lleva of: opposite the bank.

ejemplos.frase: Excuse me, how do I get to the train station?
ejemplos.traduccion: Perdone, ¿cómo llego a la estación de tren?

ejemplos.frase: Go straight on and turn right at the traffic lights.
ejemplos.traduccion: Siga todo recto y gire a la derecha en el semáforo.

ejemplos.frase: The pharmacy is between the bank and the supermarket.
ejemplos.traduccion: La farmacia está entre el banco y el supermercado.

ejemplos.frase: It's about a fifteen-minute walk from here.
ejemplos.traduccion: Está a unos quince minutos andando desde aquí.

ejemplos.frase: Is there a bus stop near the hospital?
ejemplos.traduccion: ¿Hay una parada de autobús cerca del hospital?

ejemplos.frase: We usually go to the city centre by underground.
ejemplos.traduccion: Normalmente vamos al centro en metro.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I'm going to the library to buy a novel.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I'm going to the bookshop to buy a novel.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Library means “biblioteca”; to buy books, go to a bookshop.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The bank is in front of the park.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The bank is opposite the park.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: On the other side of the street is opposite; in front of means just before something, on the same side.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I go to work by foot.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I go to work on foot.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Turn to the left in the second street.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Take the second street on the left.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Fixed phrase: take the first/second on the left/right.

ejercicios.frase: Excuse me, how do I ___ to the museum?
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives the fixed phrase “How do I get to…?” (es: ¿cómo llego a…?) for asking for directions. The clue is the structure “how do I ___ to the museum”: the verb that goes with “to” to mean reaching a place is “get”. So: “How do I get to the museum?”. “Arrive” does not work here, because it goes with “at” or “in” and is not used in this phrase.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: How do I get to…? is the question for finding a place.

errores_previstos.respuesta: arrive
errores_previstos.explicacion: “Arrive” goes with “at” or “in”, not with “to”, and does not form this phrase; to ask the way, say “How do I get to…?”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: go
errores_previstos.explicacion: “How do I go to…?” is understood, but the usual phrase for asking the way is “How do I get to…?”.

glosario.significado: Perdone, disculpe (para llamar la atención de alguien)

ejercicios.frase: Go straight ___ until you see the church.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives “go straight on / ahead” (es: seguir todo recto). The clue is “Go straight ___ until you see the church”: you continue in the same direction without turning. Both “on” (more British) and “ahead” (more general) are correct. “Straight” here means “not turning”, not a side: the side is “right”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Without turning: go straight on or go straight ahead.
ejercicios.traduccion: Siga todo recto hasta que vea la iglesia.

errores_previstos.respuesta: right
errores_previstos.explicacion: “Go straight right” does not exist; “right” is a side, and “without turning” is “straight on” or “straight ahead”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: forward
errores_previstos.explicacion: “Forward” means towards the front in general, but the fixed phrase for directions is “straight on” or “straight ahead”.

ejercicios.frase: The café is ___ the corner of Oxford Street.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives “on the corner” (es: en la esquina). The clue is “___ the corner of Oxford Street”, which places a shop where two streets meet. Both “on the corner” and “at the corner” are accepted; both say where something is. “In the corner” is something different: the corner inside a room.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Where two streets meet: on the corner (also at the corner).
ejercicios.traduccion: La cafetería está en la esquina de Oxford Street.

errores_previstos.respuesta: in
errores_previstos.explicacion: “In the corner” is the corner inside a room; a street corner is “on” or “at the corner”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: en
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the Spanish preposition; in English we say “on the corner”.

ejercicios.frase: I want to borrow some books. Where's the ___?
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the false friend the card highlights: “library” is “biblioteca” and “bookshop” is “librería”. The clue is the verb “borrow”: you borrow books from a library, not from a shop. So: “library”. If you wanted to buy them, the word would be “bookshop”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: You borrow books from a library.
ejercicios.traduccion: Quiero tomar prestados unos libros. ¿Dónde está la biblioteca?

por_opcion.library: Correct: a place where you borrow books.
por_opcion.bookshop: Incorrect here: a “bookshop” is a shop where you buy books, not borrow them.
por_opcion.bookstore: Incorrect here: it is the American form of “bookshop”, so it is also a shop.

glosario.definicion_l: a room where books are kept · a collection of literary documents or records kept for reference or borrowing

ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives “traffic lights” (es: semáforo), always plural because there are several lights. The clue is “are red”, with a plural verb, and the order “Stop!”. So: “traffic lights”. In Spanish we say “el semáforo” in the singular, but in English the plural is normal.

por_opcion.signs: Incorrect: “traffic signs” are road signs, and they do not turn red.
por_opcion.lamps: Incorrect: “lamps” are lights for a room; they do not form this expression.

glosario.definicion_l: a visual signal to control the flow of traffic at intersections

ejercicios.frase: I don't have a car, so I go everywhere ___ foot.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that means of transport go with “by” (by car, by bus), with one exception: “on foot”, walking. The clue is “___ foot” and “I don't have a car”. So: “on foot”. It is one of the card's typical mistakes: “by foot” sounds logical, but it is not the normal form.
ejercicios.traduccion: No tengo coche, así que voy a todas partes a pie.

por_opcion.on: Correct: “on foot” is the fixed expression for walking somewhere.
por_opcion.by: Incorrect: “by” goes with vehicles (by car, by train), but walking is “on foot”.
por_opcion.with: Incorrect: “with foot” does not exist; “with” means company or instrument.

ejercicios.frase: The hotel is ___ the station, just across the road.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card reminds you that “opposite” (es: enfrente de) does not take “of”: opposite the bank. The clue is “just across the road”, which describes two buildings facing each other with the street between them. So: “opposite the station”. “In front of” means just before something, on the same side, and it would also need “of”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Opposite takes no preposition after it.
ejercicios.traduccion: El hotel está enfrente de la estación, justo al otro lado de la calle.

por_opcion.opposite: Correct: “opposite” works directly as a preposition, without “of”.
por_opcion.opposite of: Incorrect: it is a calque of Spanish “enfrente de”. “The opposite of” only exists as a noun (the contrary of).
por_opcion.in front: Incorrect: it is missing “of” (“in front of”), and it means on the same side, not across the street.

glosario.definicion_l: being directly across from each other; facing · of leaves etc.; growing in pairs on either side of a stem

glosario.significado: al otro lado de la calle

ejercicios.frase: You need medicine? There's a ___ next to the bank.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives “chemist's” (British) or “pharmacy” (es: farmacia). The clue is “You need medicine?”: you buy medicine at a chemist's. Like other British shops, it is formed with the name of the professional + 's: chemist's, butcher's, baker's (the chemist's, the butcher's, the baker's shop).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: You buy medicine at the chemist's.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¿Necesitas medicinas? Hay una farmacia al lado del banco.

por_opcion.chemist's: Correct: a shop that sells medicine (British English).
por_opcion.butcher's: Incorrect: a “butcher's” is a shop that sells meat.
por_opcion.baker's: Incorrect: a “baker's” is a shop that sells bread.

glosario.definicion_l: a retail shop where medicine and other articles are sold
the branches of medical science that deal with nonsurgical techniques · (medicine) something that treats or prevents or alleviates the symptoms of disease

ejercicios.frase: We went to the city centre by foot.
respuestas: We went to the city centre on foot.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the card's exception to the rule of “by” with means of transport: walking is “on foot”, not “by foot”. The clue is “by foot”, which copies “by car” or “by bus”. The correct sentence is “We went to the city centre on foot”. In informal English people also say “We walked to the city centre”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Walking is on foot, not by foot.
ejercicios.traduccion: Fuimos al centro de la ciudad a pie.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We went to the city centre by foot.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: walking is “on foot”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We went to the city centre with foot.
errores_previstos.explicacion: “With” does not form this expression; the correct one is “on foot”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We went to the city centre on feet.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The fixed expression is singular: “on foot”.

glosario.definicion_l: the central part of a city

ejercicios.frase: The cinema is next of the bank.
respuestas: The cinema is next to the bank.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives “next to” (es: al lado de). The clue is “next of”, a calque of Spanish “al lado de”: here “de” is translated as “to”. The correct sentence is “The cinema is next to the bank”. It is a fixed compound preposition: “next to”.
ejercicios.traduccion: El cine está al lado del banco.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The cinema is next of the bank.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: Spanish “al lado de” is “next to”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The cinema is next the bank.
errores_previstos.explicacion: “To” is missing: the full preposition is “next to”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The cinema is beside of the bank.
errores_previstos.explicacion: “Beside” means the same, but it does not take “of”; also, the form asked for is “next to”.

ejercicios.frase: I bought this dictionary at the library on the corner.
respuestas: I bought this dictionary at the bookshop on the corner.
I bought this dictionary at the bookstore on the corner.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the card's false friend: a “library” is a place where you borrow books, and you do not buy books there. The clue is the verb “bought”: if you bought it, the place is a shop, a “bookshop” in British English or a “bookstore” in American English. Both are accepted. The rest of the sentence does not change.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: You do not buy books in a library: bookshop or bookstore.
ejercicios.traduccion: Compré este diccionario en la librería de la esquina.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I bought this dictionary at the library on the corner.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: a “library” lends books; the shop is a “bookshop”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I bought this dictionary at the librery on the corner.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Changing the spelling does not fix the false friend; the correct word is “bookshop”.

glosario.definicion_l: a room where books are kept · a collection of literary documents or records kept for reference or borrowing

respuestas: Take the first on the left
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the fixed phrase from the table “take the first on the right/left” to say which street to take. It starts with the imperative “Take”, with a capital letter; then the ordinal with the article, “the first”; and it ends with “on the left”. The word “street” is understood. One “the” goes before “first” and the other before “left”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Fixed phrase for saying which street to take.
ejercicios.traduccion: Coja la primera a la izquierda.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Take the left on the first
errores_previstos.explicacion: The parts are swapped: the ordinal “first” goes first and the direction, “on the left”, at the end.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Take on the left the first
errores_previstos.explicacion: This order copies Spanish “coja a la izquierda la primera”; in English it is “the first on the left”.

glosario.palabra: take the first on the left
glosario.significado: coja la primera a la izquierda

respuestas: Is there a bank near here
ejercicios.explicacion: The card uses “Is there…?” to ask if something is nearby. The clue is that you must make a question with “is” and “there”: in a question the verb goes first, “Is there”. Then comes “a bank” and finally the place expression “near here”. It is the basic question for finding a service.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Is there…? asks if something is nearby.

errores_previstos.respuesta: There is a bank near here
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is a statement (there is a bank nearby), not a question; to ask, invert: “Is there…”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Is there near here a bank
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the Spanish order “¿hay por aquí cerca un banco?”; in English the place expression goes at the end.

ejercicios.frase: Go round the ___ and take the third exit.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives “roundabout” (es: rotonda), with the example “Go round the roundabout”. The clue is “Go round the ___” and “take the third exit”: this is the typical way to give directions at a British roundabout. It is a compound word written as one, from “round” and “about”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Dé la vuelta a la rotonda y tome la tercera salida.

errores_previstos.respuesta: rotonda
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the Spanish word; in English it is “roundabout”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: round about
errores_previstos.explicacion: The noun is written as one word: “roundabout”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: crossroads
errores_previstos.explicacion: A “crossroads” is a place where streets cross, without a circle; it has no numbered exits.

glosario.definicion_l: marked by obliqueness or indirection in speech or conduct · deviating from a straight course
an opening that permits escape or release · euphemistic expressions for death

ejercicios.frase: You can get the form at the town ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives “town hall” (es: ayuntamiento), the building. The clue is “the town ___”: the word that completes the compound is “hall”, which means a large room or public building. So: “the town hall”. In big cities you also hear “city hall”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Spanish “ayuntamiento” (the building) is the town hall.
ejercicios.traduccion: Puede recoger el formulario en el ayuntamiento.

errores_previstos.respuesta: council
errores_previstos.explicacion: “Town council” is the local government as an institution (the councillors); the building where you collect a form is the “town hall”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: house
errores_previstos.explicacion: A “town house” is a terraced house in a town, not the town hall.

glosario.definicion_l: a government building that houses administrative offices of a town government
the phonological or orthographic sound or appearance of a word that can be used to describe or identify something · a category of things distinguished by some common characteristic or quality

descripcion_larga_es: Names of places in the city (bank, chemist's, town hall, library), means of transport and the phrases for asking where a place is and explaining how to get there (How do I get to…?, turn left, opposite the bank). It is survival vocabulary for any trip. It is difficult because of false friends like library (“biblioteca”, not “librería”) and prepositions that do not match Spanish (on foot, opposite without “of”).

contexto.que_es: It is the basic vocabulary for getting around a city: names of places and services, means of transport, prepositions of place (next to, opposite, between, on the corner) and the phrases for asking for and giving directions with the imperative (go straight on, turn right, take the first on the left).
contexto.por_que_importa: It is one of the first things you need when you travel or help a visitor, and it appears in all beginner-level exams. A wrong preposition or a false friend can send someone to the wrong place: if you ask for a “library” to buy a book, they will send you to a place that lends books.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: To ask where a place is (Excuse me, where is…?, Is there a… near here?), to explain a route and to locate things on a map. The signals are Excuse me, How do I get to…? and the verbs go, turn and take. Spanish speakers tend to translate “a pie” as “by foot”, “enfrente de” as “opposite of” and “librería” as “library”.
